themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 148 THIS WEEK—a 472% spike from the 25.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 14.23)—suggesting either a sudden wave of pothole formation, flooding damage, or a new street maintenance failure in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 148 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 25.9 weekly baseline (472% spike, z-score 14.23)
Corroborating spike in street sweeping complaints: 5 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 baseline (1900% spike)
565 DOB permit filings in past 90 days suggest active construction/ground disturbance may be factor
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent heavy weather (snow/ice 3 weeks ago) exposed underlying street maintenance backlog; interview DOT about repair timeline
Map the geographic cluster of complaints—are they concentrated near a single intersection, development site, or utility work zone?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK from a 0.1 weekly average (3100% spike, z-score: 11.72)—suggesting coordinated graffiti tagging, campaign poster saturation, or a newly unmonitored corridor in the district.
evidence: 4 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3100% spike, z-score 11.72)
Illegal fireworks spike 2033% three weeks ago suggests possible event-driven or seasonal uptick in disorder complaints
No recent Reddit or news mentions indicate issue is flying under media radar despite statistical severity
reporting_angles: Photograph complaint hotspots and interview residents on Sunnyside Ave, Queens Blvd, or near transit hubs about recent poster/graffiti appearance
Contact 311 to determine if spike reflects actual increase or change in complaint-filing behavior post-awareness campaign

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Canopy Loss
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints hit 24 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 967% spike from the 2.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 11.33)—likely linked to the 1,053 snow/ice complaints recorded over the past 90 days, indicating widespread branch failure or storm damage to Sunnyside's street tree inventory.
evidence: 24 damaged tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.2 weekly baseline (967% spike, z-score 11.33)
1,053 snow/ice complaints across 90-day period (third-highest complaint category) directly correlates with winter branch damage
Community board budget requests include repeated calls for park/amenity expansion, suggesting tree canopy/green space is an unsolved chronic issue
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept. about emergency tree removal backlog and timeline for replanting in Sunnyside; obtain damage assessment data
Locate residents with photos of downed branches or obstructed sidewalks; assess public safety risk from unstable trees near schools/residential blocks

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Infrastructure Failure
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal condition complaints jumped to 175 LAST WEEK—a 307% spike from the 43.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.8)—indicating a potential widespread signal outage, electrical failure, or timing dysfunction affecting commute and pedestrian safety across the district.
evidence: 175 traffic signal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 43.0 weekly baseline (307% spike, z-score 6.8)
Traffic signal condition is already the 5th highest complaint category over 90 days (855 total), suggesting chronic underinvestment
Multiple ULURP rezonings and development projects (21-31 46th Ave, 50-02 Queens Blvd, Hunters Point Ave) may have triggered infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DOT to determine if recent signal failures were caused by weather, power disruptions, or failed infrastructure upgrades
Map complaint cluster geographically—focus on major intersections (Queens Blvd, Roosevelt Ave, 39th Ave) to identify if outage was localized or district-wide

themes_detail.label: Animal & Sanitary Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal complaints and unsanitary condition complaints hit 3 and 6 respectively THIS WEEK—unprecedented spikes (2300% and 300% increases)—suggesting either a pest infestation, illicit dumping hotspot, or failed building code enforcement.
evidence: 3 unsanitary animal (private property) complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 baseline (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
3 'outside building' sanitation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 baseline (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
262 unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days (tenth-highest category) indicates baseline sanitation challenges
reporting_angles: Identify the specific blocks with animal complaints using 311 open data portal; inspect for rodent activity, pet hoarding, or illegal animal operations
Cross-reference with DOB violations and HPD complaints to determine if property owners are neglecting maintenance standards
